summary: Verified full FCM-only refactor. 12/12 backend regression tests passed against the public URL covering health, admin login (email_or_phone/HeartLink@2026), /api/admin/push/status (provider=fcm, configured=true, can_send_notifications=true, users_with_fcm_token>0), /api/admin/push/test (success=true), /api/admin/push/send target=all, /api/fcm/register-token, backward-compat /api/admin/onesignal/{status,send,test} (all route to FCM with provider=fcm), /api/admin/daily-notification-status (scheduler_running=true), /api/admin/notifications/templates (non-empty templates dict), /api/notifications/{user_id}. Frontend compiles with 0 errors (only non-blocking source-map warnings for @capacitor-community/admob & google-auth). Landing page loads, title 'HeartLink...', SW registers, no OneSignal script/globals injected, no console errors. Verified /app/frontend/src/services/oneSignalService.js is DELETED and no remaining imports reference it (grep clean). pushNotifications.js contains Capacitor.isNativePlatform() guard, PushNotifications.checkPermissions/requestPermissions (Android 13+), PushNotifications.register, registration/registrationError/pushNotificationReceived/pushNotificationActionPerformed listeners, LocalNotifications.createChannel + localNotificationActionPerformed for deep-link routing, and TAG-based debug logging.

issues: UI copy still says 'Send via OneSignal' / uses handleSendViaOneSignal/handleTestOneSignal names and comments — functionally fine (calls backward-compat endpoints which route to FCM) but naming/labels are misleading given OneSignal removal. Recommend renaming to 'Send via FCM' for user-facing clarity.

action_items: Optional: Rename NotificationManager.jsx handlers/labels from OneSignal→FCM and migrate its axios calls to /api/admin/push/* (current /api/admin/onesignal/* still works via aliases).
Optional cleanup: Legacy test files test_onesignal*.py under /app/backend/tests could be removed or renamed since OneSignal was removed.
critical_code_review_comments: Backward-compat aliases correctly forward to FCM handlers — no code duplication.

/api/admin/push/send has a subtle logic issue: it always runs admin_broadcast first, then overrides result with send_to_users only when target=='user_ids'. For target=='user_ids', a broadcast to ALL users is still executed before the targeted send, causing an unintended global push. Recommend early return on target=='user_ids'.
fcm_service.is_fcm_ready() drives both 'configured' and 'can_send_notifications' — fine, but consider exposing token-freshness metric (active vs stale) in /admin/push/status.
server.py is 7435 lines — well over the 700-line guideline; consider modularizing (routers already partly split via new_features_endpoints.py).

success_rate.frontend: compile+load OK; deep UI flow not exercised (admin panel login not automated this run)
